result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both plans use a 3×3 small-multiple grid, sort panels by current-year sales, and put month labels only on the bottom row. A is the stronger quarterly figure: one shared zero-based scale unless a dominant line is split out with a visible note and a size cue, plus a partial current year and a marked quarter. B is tighter and more selective about accents, but it treats separate y-axes as the normal case whenever sizes differ, which weakens the volume comparison. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both plans use a 3×3 small-multiples grid ordered by current-year sales, with prior years in gray and the current quarter shaded. B is the stronger review figure: a shared zero-based scale is the default, any split is labeled in the subtitle and backed by share or YoY, and the current year is drawn only through reported months. A meets the small-multiples brief with selective highlighting and direct labels, while making separate y-axes the usual choice once line sizes diverge.
